ctx.x: George, can you tell, who else was in the band? Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone, Lee Collins on trumpet, and with the addition of Buddy, maybe we had two trumpets for us. Yes.

And a seven-piece arch. Well, now in this story, it's slightly different from the story I've had before, because I've heard that you played with Buddy, or he played with you in George Orson's song. Then you had some kind of a, you know, Buddy didn't get on with Buddy or something, and you fired Buddy, and you got Lee Collins after Buddy left. No, I don't remember that.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: I worked in that place two years, man. Me and Lee and Sonny Andy. Roy Evans. Joe Robeshoe. And Plekton. Rennie Hall. That's all we had.

ctx.x: They had one here, but I never want to go there. Why, that's... Yeah, I did see one one time. I was looking for Rene, and I went to this Cadillac Club down on St. Claude, and they had one there, you know. But I never paid attention to it, you know. I'd rather listen to the music and find the girls later.

Man, them cats are taking... You buy a dollar worth of tickets over there that day when you come in. Girls sitting all up there now. With a dollar worth of... Ten cents a dance. But a girl got a string of tickets about that long. Still at the bottom, see. Boy, now they got a guy walk around. Take them tickets from, you know. Girl got the tickets. She done snapped it off. Mm-hmm. You get it this end. Banner stop, you know. Time for another snap-off ticket. Well, they even made this round. That's two free…
